messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the monoclinic space group P2₁/m (space-group number 11, Hall symbol –P 2yb). The original input cell is not the conventional setting: its lattice parameters are a = 4.250922 Å, b = 10.164177 Å, c = 13.14184385 Å, with α = 85.38147959°, β = 90.0°, and γ = 90.0°, and it contains 20 atoms with the declared input composition Ba₄In₈P₈. Fractional coordinates are used throughout, and the standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix has first row (0, −1, 0), second row (1, 6.300350718748151×10⁻¹⁷, 0), and third row (2.9104969247691962×10⁻¹⁸, 1.2024605197811162×10⁻¹⁷, 1), with origin shift s = (0, 0.5, 0). Thus, to recover the original input geometry from the standard description, one applies the inverse of this near-axis-exchange transformation, whose small off-diagonal terms reflect the slight monoclinic inclination of the input cell.

In the standard frame, all atoms lie on mirror-related 2e positions of the form (x, 1/4, z), so the structure is built from ten independent two-fold orbits, each with one atom at y = 1/4 and its symmetry mate generated by the monoclinic symmetry. Barium occupies two inequivalent orbits: Ba at x = 0.438959, z = 0.153972, and a second Ba orbit at x = 0.840089, z = 0.591147. Indium occupies four inequivalent orbits: In at x = 0.447726, z = 0.594965; In at x = 0.043782, z = 0.164902; In at x = 0.810984, z = 0.035439; and In at x = 0.227766, z = 0.716874. Phosphorus likewise occupies four inequivalent orbits: P at x = 0.800271, z = 0.833946; P at x = 0.392158, z = 0.393144; P at x = 0.921415, z = 0.338338; and P at x = 0.329379, z = 0.910597. All positional values are given to six decimal places, and no additional precision corrections are required beyond this rounding.
